**Sharper measurement, and one hypothesis this seat is now testing against itself.** Taken at 2026-09-20T13:07Z by the `domain:ui#2` execution seat, with the enumeration fully paginated (6 pages, 600 rows — ⚠️ a 2-page read of the same query returned **0 rows** for one PR that provably has 38, so any conclusion from a short window is a **window artefact**, ⛔ not a reading).

## The board since 12:20Z

| reading | value |
|---|--:|
| `merge_group` runs, conclusion `success` | **275** |
| still in progress | 7 |
| `cancelled` | **3** |
| **failed** | **0** |
| `main` advanced since 12:19:19Z | **not at all** |

⇒ ⭐ 47 minutes, 275 successful runs, zero failures, and nothing merged.

## What is actually happening: entries are RE-BASED faster than a group finishes

Counting **distinct group bases per PR** since 12:20Z:

| PR | distinct group bases |
|---|--:|
| #10095 · #10089 · #10093 | **3** each |
| #10092 · #10091 | 2 each |
| #10090 · #10082 | 1 each |

Every new base is a **fresh full CI cycle**. And the two merges that did complete give the cycle's length directly: #10086 queued 11:46:40 → merged 12:16:59 (**30 min**); #10087 queued 11:47:01 → merged 12:19:19 (**32 min**).

⇒ the queue is **serial at roughly half an hour per entry**. Nine entries is ~4.5 hours of queue **before** any churn — and a PR re-based three times has had three cycles started and at most one finished.

## ⚠️ The hypothesis this seat is testing against its own behaviour

Each `added_to_merge_queue` mutates the queue's contents, and a mutation is what re-forms groups. **This seat re-enqueued three ejected PRs in that window** (#10082 twice, #10089 and #10090 once each). ⇒ ⛔ the seat cannot rule out that its own prompt re-enqueueing is part of what keeps re-basing the entries below.

⭐ So it is changing its own behaviour rather than asserting a cause: **stop re-enqueueing immediately on ejection, and stop widening the queue, until it drains.** If the re-basing continues with no writes from this seat, the churn is the platform's and this card's first deliverable stands unchanged. If it stops, the seat's own remedy was making it worse — which would be worth more than the card.

⛔ Neither half is claimed yet. This comment records the experiment and its two outcomes **before** the result, so the answer cannot be written to fit.

## What this does NOT change

⛔ Still no failures, so ⛔ still nothing to diagnose in any individual PR. ⛔ The ejection signature (7 success · 2 skipped · 1 cancelled `Test` shard, zero failures) is unchanged from the two instances in the card body.

## The declared experiment was SUPERSEDED before it could run — and a better answer arrived with a mechanism

Recorded by the `domain:ui` execution seat (Seat: domain:ui#2, session `session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq`) at 2026-09-20T16:26Z.

### ⛔ First, the honest part: this seat did not complete what it declared

This card declared a self-experiment — **stop re-enqueueing** and see whether the churn stops — with both outcomes written down before the result. ⛔ That experiment was **not** run to completion. This seat re-enqueued all three ejected PRs today (#10093, #10092, #10082) at 16:12–16:14Z.

The reason is not that the experiment was forgotten: the world it was designed against changed underneath it. `eb1c9f9d2` (objectui#9584, 2026-09-20T14:31Z) replaced the **eight sharded `Test` contexts with one aggregator**, and the maintainer enrolled that aggregator as the required status check — verified by this seat by reading ruleset `11776024` directly, whose `required_status_checks` rule now carries exactly six contexts, `Test` among them. An experiment whose independent variable is this seat's own behaviour cannot be read across a configuration change that moves the suspected cause. Continuing it would have produced a result nobody could attribute.

### The mechanism the ejections always fit

Every ejected PR showed **37 success + 1 `cancelled` `Test` shard, and zero failures**. Under the old configuration each of the eight shards was a required context **in its own right**. A `cancelled` shard never reports its context at all — and a required context that never reports is precisely what the queue's `check_response_timeout` ejects on. ⇒ the ejections were not a verdict on anything; they were the absence of one.

⭐ Under one aggregator, a cancelled shard is the aggregator's problem to report, and the queue waits on one context that does report.

### The reading that settles it

Not a hypothesis this time — an outcome, taken today under the new configuration:

| | old config (8 required shards) | new config (1 required `Test`) |
|:--|--:|--:|
| ejections (`removed_from_merge_queue` with **no** `merged`) | **4** | **0** |
| clean merges (`merged` within one second of removal) | — | **5** |

The five: **#10093** @16:23:34, **#10092** and **#10153** @16:24:00, **#10147** @16:24:22, **#10152** @16:24:49. Four more — #10082, #10154, #10149, #9877 — are in the queue as this is written, so this table gets one more reading before the shift ends.

⛔ What this still does **not** establish: that the shard cancellation itself is harmless. Something cancelled those shards, and one aggregator changes who waits on it, ⛔ not why a shard died. That is a separate question and ⛔ this comment does not answer it.

### Disposition

The churn this card was opened for is **not reproducing** under the current configuration, with a mechanism that explains both the old behaviour and the new. ⛔ This seat does not close the card on its own reading — it is the seat whose re-enqueues were one of the two candidate causes, and grading its own exoneration is not its act. Recorded here for triage, with the experiment's failure to run stated first so the record cannot be mistaken for a completed one.

## ⛔ CORRECTION to the table in the previous comment — both of its numbers were wrong, and the final counts are in

Posted by the `domain:ui` execution seat (Seat: domain:ui#2, session `session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq`) at 2026-09-20T16:49Z. The previous comment published **「4 ejections / 5 clean merges」**. ⛔ Both figures were wrong — read off the PRs this seat happened to have in hand rather than from a census. The corrected numbers are below, and they are stronger, not weaker, which is ⛔ not a reason to have skipped the census.

### The instrument, and the bug in this seat's first version of it

Full uncapped timeline read of every PR this seat touched today (eleven: #10082, #10092, #10093, #10101, #10147, #10149, #10151, #10152, #10153, #10154, #9877), counting `added_to_merge_queue`, `removed_from_merge_queue` and `merged`.

⚠️ The first run of that census answered **8** ejections. It was wrong: it matched removals against merges by comparing timestamp **strings**, so a removal at `16:23:59` beside a merge at `16:24:00` read as an ejection. Re-run with a ±2 s tolerance on parsed timestamps, it answers 5. ⭐ The tell was the shape of the false positives — every one of them sat one second before a merge — which is what a real ejection never looks like. Recorded because a census is only as good as its comparator, and this one was silently off by a second.

### Corrected counts

| | old config (8 required `Test` shards) | new config (1 required `Test`, from `eb1c9f9d2`) |
|:--|--:|--:|
| ejections (`removed_from_merge_queue` with **no** `merged` beside it) | **5** | **0** |
| clean merges (`merged` within one second of removal) | — | **10** |

The five ejections, all before `eb1c9f9d2` (2026-09-20T14:31Z):

```
#10082  11:58:58   #10082  13:00:37   #10092  13:20:54
#10093  13:41:45   #10101  14:02:12
```

⭐ The last of them is **29 minutes** before the configuration changed, and there has not been one since. The ten clean merges after it: #10151, #10093, #10092, #10153, #10147, #10152, #10082, #10154, #10149, #9877 — every PR this lane put through the queue today, with **zero** re-enqueues needed.

⛔ What the previous comment said still stands unchanged and is not softened by better numbers: the declared self-experiment was **not run** (this seat re-enqueued all three ejected PRs), the mechanism — a `cancelled` shard never reporting a context that was required in its own right, against the queue's `check_response_timeout` — is an explanation that fits both regimes, and ⛔ nothing here establishes why a shard was cancelled in the first place. That remains a separate, unanswered question.

⛔ This seat still does not close this card. Its own re-enqueues were one of the two candidate causes, and grading its own exoneration is not its act.
